episodes.202895: A moist and unstable summer airmass led to the development of scattered afternoon thunderstorms, a few of which were strong to severe.
episodes.202921: Daytime heating resulted in the development of showers and thunderstorms across the higher terrain, including the Sacramento Mountains, Storms over the Sacramento Mountains built north over Ruidoso and the South Fork burn scar early afternoon with rainfall amounts of around 0.5 to 1 inch in 20 minutes over the burn scar. This resulted in some flash flooding and minor debris flows on neighbor roadways in and around the burn scar, leading to some brief closures. Storms moved west of the burn scar and Sacramento Mountains shortly afterwards with any closed roads reopened by the mid afternoon. Elsewhere, an evening thunderstorm brought a brief 58 mph wind gust to the mesonet station at I-25 at Rowe.
episodes.202930: Scattered thunderstorms produced isolated strong winds and damage across central and north-central South Dakota during the evening of July 14th. A collapsing storm produced 82 mph winds measured by the Pierre Regional Airport Automated Surface Observing System, resulting in tree and vehicle damage on the east side of town. Another storm west of Onida would go on to topple multiple powerlines with an estimated 100 mph wind gust. Multiple reports of wind gusts of 50 to 70 mph were observed through the evening and overnight hours. As the thunderstorms departed, a second round of strong, non-thunderstorm winds followed the system overnight into July 15th.
episodes.203021: An anomalously moist airmass with tropical moisture resided over much of Virginia on July 15th. Another round of slow moving thunderstorms developed on remnant boundaries and terrain circulations before propagating eastward. These thunderstorms moved into areas with suppressed flash flood guidance due to anteceding conditions. Ultimately, these storms produced localized rainfall amounts of two to five inches.
episodes.203061: A line of thunderstorms moved through the southern Nebraska panhandle, causing strong wind gusts in Cheyenne County.
episodes.203136: Another day of an anomalously moist airmass produced numerous showers and thunderstorms across Virginia. This resulted in localized rainfall amounts of 2 to 4 inches in a short period of time, which resulted in instances of flooding and flash flooding.
episodes.203175: Another day of an anomalously moist airmass produced numerous showers and thunderstorms across Maryland. This resulted in localized rainfall amounts of 2 to 4 inches in a short period of time, which resulted in instances of flooding and flash flooding.
episodes.203224: Slow-moving thunderstorms brought heavy rain and scattered flash flooding to western interior southern New England.
episodes.203808: Isolated thunderstorms developed along the bay breeze.
episodes.203934: A weak northern stream shortwave trough moving through the northwest CONUS resulted in the development of high based convection. Some of this convection resulted in strong to severe wind gusts. Additionally, a cutoff low placed off of the southwest CONUS helped advect moisture into southern Utah, leading to convection with periods of sufficiently heavy rain to result in flash flooding over some rain sensitive areas.
episodes.203938: A weak northern stream shortwave trough moving through the northwest CONUS resulted in the development of high based convection. Some of this convection resulted in strong to severe wind gusts in southwest Wyoming.
episodes.203943: A hot and humid air mass combined with orographical lift to produce isolated severe thunderstorms across southwest Virginia. Damaging wind gusts from these storms blew down a few trees in Franklin and Henry counties, and lightning from these storms struck a house in both Franklin and Roanoke counties and set them on fire.
episodes.203968: A hot and humid air mass combined with orographical lift to produce a severe thunderstorm in Pulaski County of southwest Virginia. Damaging wind gusts from this storm impacted a roof of a building and a greenhouse about one mile west of Allisonia.
episodes.203969: A hot and humid air mass combined with orographical lift to produce a severe thunderstorm in Surry County of northwest North Carolina. Damaging wind gusts from this storm blew down three trees. In addition, lightning from a different storm struck the Winstead Pumping Station in Reidsville and damaged the generator transfer switch and central panel, which led to nearly 4,200 gallons of untreated sewage being released into Lick Fork Creek.
episodes.204626: A broad surface low moved east to west across north Florida through the day. This feature combined with surface instability, high moisture, weak shear and sea breezes produced locally heavy rainfall.
episodes.204720: Isolated to scattered showers and storms developed along the border with southeastern Virginia in the afternoon hours. The storms then propagated south and southwest during the evening hours. Several reports of flooding were observed, along with a few wind damage reports.
episodes.204824: A summertime pattern continued over the area with scattered thunderstorms. There were several reports of strong wind gusts in excess of 34 knots.
episodes.205008: A mesoscale convective vortex developed over northern Mexico and sent an outflow boundary into South-Central Texas. Thunderstorms in this complex produced locally heavy rain that led to flash flooding.
episodes.205122: A moist and unstable summer airmass led to the development of scattered afternoon thunderstorms, a few of which were strong to severe.
episodes.205201: A few thunderstorms developed during the morning hours of the 15th along a stationary boundary draped across central Minnesota from west to east. A few of these storms produced large hail along with some isolated tree damage in east-central Minnesota.
episodes.205202: A stationary boundary was draped across western Wisconsin during the day on the 15th. This led to multiple rounds of storms across northwestern Wisconsin during the morning and afternoon hours. Some of the storms contained damaging winds that led to tree damage across parts of Washburn, Sawyer, Ashland, and Bayfield counties.
episodes.205203: A stationary boundary was draped across western Wisconsin during the day on the 15th. This led to multiple rounds of storms across northwestern Wisconsin during the morning and afternoon hours. Some of the storms contained damaging winds across the Chequamegon Bay area during the day with a maximum gust of 52 mph recorded at the roundabout four miles west of Ashland on US2.
episodes.205255: Severe thunderstorms produced large hail across parts of eastern North Dakota during the late evening and early morning hours.
episodes.205312: A moist and unstable air mass was in place from July 14 through July 15. This allowed for widespread, slow-moving storms to move across portions of central, southern, and southeastern Virginia. These storms produced heavy rain and widespread flash flooding in two rounds. One round was from overnight convection on the night of July 14 into the morning of July 15 and the other round was during the afternoon of July 15. Widespread rainfall totals of 2-4 inches were observed across south-central and southern Virginia as well as the Northern Neck with localized totals of 5-7 inches between eastern Dinwiddie County to western Surry County. The highest measured total was 7.33 inches from the Petersburg, Dinwiddie County Airport ASOS/AWOS. Given the very heavy rainfall and saturated soil leading up to the event, a flash flood emergency was issued in Petersburg on the night of July 14 through the morning of July 15.
episodes.205313: A moist and unstable air mass was in place on July 15. This allowed for scattered, slow-moving storms to move across portions of interior northeast North Carolina. These storms produced heavy rain and flash flooding.
episodes.205330: Thunderstorms during the afternoon produced flooding in Aberdeen. A separate storm that formed along the Missouri River north of Oacoma was responsible for a waterspout.
episodes.205339: A moist and unstable air mass was in place on July 15. This allowed for widespread, slow-moving storms to move across portions of central, southern, and southeastern Virginia. An isolated storm become severe and produced damaging winds across southern Virginia.
episodes.205423: A frontal boundary slowly progressed south during the afternoon and early evening hours. Scattered instances of severe wind gusts were witnessed in conjunction with storms that developed along the boundary. The most concentrated damage was reported across Meeker, Stearns, and Sherburne counties.
episodes.205431: An isolated pulse thunderstorm moves slowly over portions o the Springfield metro causing flooding in the Fassnight Creek and Park areas. Rain in excess of an inch fell in a 15 minute period.
episodes.205436: Thunderstorms developed south of an approaching cold front and in the vicinity of a surface trough of low pressure during the late afternoon hours of July 15th. Activity developed in Grant and southern Cherry County around 3 PM MDT and quickly became severe. Thunderstorm coverage became more widespread into the evening hours as activity tracked into the central and eastern Sandhills, as well as portions of north central Nebraska. One tornado was reported north of Mullen along with hail up to 2 inches in diameter and thunderstorm wind gusts up to 65 MPH.
episodes.205490: A weak front approached from the west along with PW of 2 inches resulting in heavy rainfall across the area. 4 to 6.5 inches of rainfall totals were reported with rainfall rates between 1 to 2 inches.
episodes.205581: A stationary boundary was positioned on the northern edge of the Quad State region throughout the 14th. Early morning showers and storms moving eastward across Western Kentucky produced a small funnel cloud. Late afternoon into the evening, additional storms developed as a shortwave moved through. Torrential rainfall over Henderson led to significant flash flooding issues late evening in the city.
episodes.205582: A morning frontal boundary on the northern edge of the Quad State lifted a little northward during the day on the 15th. A 40-50kt jet out of the WSW continued into the Quad State, bringing enough Gulf moisture to keep PWATs over 2 inches. MLCAPE values reached 2000-2500J/kg, while effective bulk shear remained limited. In Southwest Indiana, scattered showers and thunderstorms occurred through the day. A funnel cloud was observed from Poseyville midday, while brief flooding occurred late afternoon in Boonville.
episodes.205584: A morning frontal boundary on the northern edge of the Quad State lifted a little northward during the day on the 15th. A 40-50kt jet out of the WSW continued into the Quad State, bringing enough Gulf moisture to keep PWATs over 2 inches. MLCAPE values reached 2000-2500J/kg, while effective bulk shear remained limited. In Southeast Missouri, scattered showers and thunderstorms occurred through the day. A funnel cloud was observed with a storm over Neelyville.
episodes.205599: A weak front approached from the west along with PW of 2 inches resulting in heavy rainfall across the area. 4 to 6.5 inches of rainfall totals were reported with rainfall rates between 1 to 2 inches.
episodes.205758: A weak frontal boundary sagged south toward the area during the afternoon/evening. Scattered to numerous thunderstorms initially developed to the north (near that boundary) and also to the west along higher terrain. The environment ahead of the boundary was characterized by very weak deep-layer flow and anomalously high PW values on the order of 2.1-2.2, leading to slow-moving storms with very heavy rainfall.
episodes.205759: A weak frontal boundary sagged south toward the area during the afternoon/evening. Scattered to numerous thunderstorms initially developed to the north (near that boundary) and also to the west along higher terrain. The environment ahead of the boundary was characterized by very weak deep-layer flow and anomalously high PW values on the order of 2.1-2.2, leading to slow-moving storms with very heavy rainfall and isolated gusty winds.
episodes.205832: An upper level low moved across Wyoming and brought a round of strong to severe thunderstorms to western and central Wyoming. The severe thunderstorms brought both hail and strong wind. The maximum wind gust reported was 75 mph near Muddy Gap with wind gusts over 58 mph also reported in Sublette, Sweetwater, Lincoln and Hot Springs Counties. In Afton, trees were blown onto power lines leading a power outage. A pile of loose rocks was blown down near Tabletop Mountain in Johnson County. In Fremont County, a supercell thunderstorm moved southeast dropping penny to ping pong size hail, with the largest hail reported to the northwest of Lander.
episodes.205849: Widespread thunderstorm damage and severe wind speeds occurred on the 15th.
episodes.205918: Showers and thunderstorms developed in the vicinity of a surface boundary stretching through central North Dakota. A few of these storms became severe. The strongest wind gusts were reported in Bowdon area of Wells County. Estimated 80 mph winds combined with hail up to one-inch in diameter to cause additional damage to homes and vehicles in Bowdon, which were already significantly damaged from storms that passed through earlier in the summer. In addition, some trees were uprooted and broken around town. The largest hail report was two inches in diameter, which occurred near Ellendale in Dickey County.
episodes.205982: A robust squall line developed across the Black Hills and moved east across the entire CWA. SD Mesonet stations recorded the extreme wind gusts with multiple sites hitting between 80-90 mph.
episodes.206008: A ridge of high pressure over the Desert Southwest was slowly pulling moisture into the region from the west with several shortwave disturbances moving across the north. This along with diurnal heating resulted in a few thunderstorms with strong gusty winds as the low levels remain very dry. One particular storm over the Eastern Uinta Mountains produced outflow winds up to 59 mph at Vernal Regional Airport.
episodes.206068: Isolated diurnally driven thunderstorms moved southwest across central Georgia. A couple storms were able to produce gusty winds and felled trees onto homes in the Butts County area.
episodes.206134: An approaching cold front sparked off showers and thunderstorms across the forecast area. Flash flooding resulted.
episodes.206153: An approaching cold front sparked off showers and thunderstorms across the forecast area. Flash flooding resulted.
episodes.206163: A cluster of thunderstorms rapidly developed across south-central South Dakota during the late afternoon on July 15 in response to an eastward moving cold front. These thunderstorms quickly expanded into a line and moved across southeast South Dakota into the mid-late evening, reaching the I-29 corridor by 2000 CST. While a few thunderstorms produced hail up to 1.25 inches in diameter, the primary hazard was severe downburst winds, gusting up to 77 mph and producing sporadic tree and structural damage. The thunderstorms weakened below severe limits upon entering Minnesota and Iowa.

The Virginia Department of Emergency Management in collaboration with the National Weather Service in Wakefield Virginia conducted a Virginia Incident Damage Assessment for the City of Petersburg after significant flooding on the night of July 14 into the morning of July 15. Widespread rainfall totals of 3-5 inches were observed across Petersburg with one report of 7.33 inches from the Petersburg, Dinwiddie County Airport ASOS/AWOS. The damage assessment found 38 damaged commercial buildings with a combined estimated damage of $3,863,288 and 16 damaged residential buildings with an estimated damage of $897,205. There was major damage to 9 commercial properties and 2 residential properties as well as minor damage to 14 commercial properties and 8 residential properties. The remainder of the properties noted above were affected by the flood waters, but were below minor damage criteria.
